  13. When reading a key via get, the cache first looks up the entry in the Map.
  14. If no entry exists, get returns undefined immediately.
  15. If an entry exists, the cache compares its expiration timestamp against the current time.
  16. When the current time is greater than or equal to the expiration timestamp, the entry is expired.
  17. An expired entry is deleted from the Map, and get returns undefined.
  18. If the entry is still alive, get refreshes its recency by moving it to the tail of the Map.
  19. Moving an entry in a Map is done by deleting the key and immediately re-inserting it.
  20. A separate peek operation reads the live value without deleting or re-inserting the key.
  21. Similarly, has, size, and keys inspect liveness without changing the recency order.
  22. When writing a key via set, the cache computes the new expiration timestamp.
  23. If the key already exists in the Map, it is deleted first so re-insertion moves it to the tail.
  24. Updating an existing key therefore counts as a recent use and resets its TTL.
  25. If the key is new and the cache is already at maximum capacity, eviction is required.
  26. Before evicting a live entry, the cache scans and removes all currently expired entries.
  27. Purging expired entries first avoids unnecessarily dropping valid data when stale items exist.
  28. If the cache is still at capacity after purging expired entries, LRU eviction runs.
  29. The cache reads the first key yielded by the Map iterator, which is the least recently used.
  30. That oldest key is deleted from the Map to free one slot for the incoming entry.
  31. Finally, the new key and its entry record are inserted at the tail of the Map.
  32. Because expiration is checked lazily on access and before eviction, no background timers are needed.
  33. Lazy expiration avoids timer overhead and prevents dangling handles from keeping processes alive.
  34. However, size and keys must also purge expired entries before reporting their results.
  35. Otherwise, callers would observe phantom expired keys in the reported count or key list.
  36. Calling keys can return live keys in most-recently-used-first order by reversing the Map keys.
  37. Deleting a key explicitly removes it from the Map regardless of its expiration status.
  38. Per-entry TTL overrides allow hot or volatile items to expire sooner or later than the default.
  39. Together, O(1) Map operations and lazy TTL checks keep common reads and writes fast.
  40. This combination provides predictable memory usage, freshness guarantees, and simple semantics.
